topics.name: Joining words: and, but, or, because

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct tense.
options: The skipper fill his cup last night.
The skipper filling his cup last night.
The skipper filled his cup last night.
questions.rule: Last night is in the past, so use the simple past: filled.

options: The moon looks like an old boat.
The moon looks like a old boat.
The moon looks like an boat.
questions.rule: Old begins with a vowel sound, so say an old boat. Boat alone takes a.

options: There are many stars in the Milky Way.
There is many stars in the Milky Way.
There am many stars in the Milky Way.
questions.rule: Stars is plural, so use There are.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: is
am
be

questions.rule: A big moon is one thing, so use There is.

howling
howls

questions.rule: Last night is in the past, so the verb takes -ed: howled.

options: an
a
many
questions.rule: Drink begins with a consonant sound, so use a.

options: spill
spilled
spilling
questions.rule: Yesterday shows the past, so use spilled.
Seven stars is plural, so we say There are.

chat: What did you see in the sky last night?
options: I see the full moon and many stars.
I seen the full moon and many stars.
I saw the full moon and many stars.
questions.rule: The question is about last night, so answer in the simple past: I saw.

chat: What did you see in the sky last night?
options: I saw a orange moon.
I saw an oranges moon.
I saw an orange moon.
questions.rule: Orange begins with a vowel sound, so say an orange moon.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct joining word.
options: He tried to drink the milk, because he spilled it.
He tried to drink the milk, but he spilled it.
He tried to drink the milk, or he spilled it.
questions.rule: But joins two ideas that go against each other: he tried, but it went wrong.

options: The skipper maked a big mistake.
The skipper made a big mistake.
The skipper did made a big mistake.
questions.rule: Make is irregular. Its past form is made, not maked.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: filling
fills
filled

questions.rule: Both actions happened in the past: dipped ... and filled.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: are
am
was

questions.rule: Two bears is plural, so use There are.

options: or
but
because
questions.rule: Use or to give a choice between two things.

options: a
many
an
questions.rule: Owl begins with a vowel sound, so use an.
Subject + past verb + object + place: Raju spilled milk on his shirt.
An goes before the vowel sound in old; a goes before bear.

chat: Look up! What can you see?
options: There is a bright star near the moon.
There are a bright star near the moon.
There is a bright stars near the moon.
questions.rule: One star: There is a bright star.

chat: Why is your shirt wet, Kabir?
options: I spill water on it at lunch today.
I spilled water on it at lunch today.
I spilling water on it at lunch today.
questions.rule: Lunch is already over, so use the simple past: spilled.

questions.prompt: Pick the sentence with the correct joining word.
options: The man wanted milk but he was thirsty.
The man wanted milk because he was thirsty.
The man wanted milk or he was thirsty.
questions.rule: Because gives the reason: he wanted milk because he was thirsty.

options: He taked an empty cup and filled it.
He took a empty cup and filled it.
He took an empty cup and filled it.
questions.rule: Past of take is took; empty begins with a vowel sound, so an empty cup.

options: There are some bread on the plate.
There is some bread on the plate.
There is some breads on the plate.
questions.rule: Bread cannot be counted, so it has no plural and takes There is.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: runs
running
ran

questions.rule: The story is in the past (frightened), so run becomes ran.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: were
is
are

questions.rule: Last night needs the past, and many clouds is plural: there were.

questions.before: When the Big Bear growled, the man
options: drop
dropped
drops
questions.rule: Growled is past, so the other action is past too: dropped.

questions.after: no milk left in the cup.
options: are
am
is
questions.rule: Milk cannot be counted, so use There is.
Because joins the event to its reason.

chat: What is that bright thing in the sky?
options: It is a aeroplane, not a star.
It is an aeroplane, not a star.
It is an aeroplane, not an star.
questions.rule: An before the vowel sound in aeroplane; a before star.

chat: Shall we watch the moon from the roof or the garden?
options: Let's go to the roof because it is higher.
Let's go to the roof but it is higher.
Let's go to the roof or it is higher.
questions.rule: We are giving a reason, so the joining word is because.

options: Both bear howled at the man.
Both bears howling at the man.
Both bears howled at the man.
questions.rule: Both needs a plural noun (bears), and the sentence needs a past verb: howled.

options: The moon is a brightest object in the night sky.
The moon is the brightest object in the night sky.
The moon is the brighter object in the night sky.
questions.rule: The -est form compares with all others and always takes the: the brightest.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: I
myself
mine

questions.rule: The doers of the action take I, not me: Riya and I watched.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: dropping
drops
dropped

questions.rule: Both parts joined by because are in the past: fell ... dropped.

questions.before: The cup belongs to Kabir. It is
options: him
his
he
questions.rule: To show that something belongs to a boy, use his.

options: is
am
are
questions.rule: Children is the plural of child, so use There are.
She does the action; me receives it.
To ask, put are before there: Are there any ...?

options: It is mine. My uncle gave it to me.
It is my. My uncle gave it to me.
It is mine. My uncle gave it to I.
questions.rule: Use mine without a noun after it, and me after to.

chat: Is there any milk in the fridge?
options: Yes, there is some milk in the jug.
Yes, there are some milk in the jug.
Yes, there is some milks in the jug.
questions.rule: Milk cannot be counted: no plural, and use there is.

options: When the bears growl, the frightened man spilled all the milk.
When the bears growled, the frightened man spilled all the milk.
When the bears growled, the frightened man spilled all the milks.
questions.rule: Keep both actions in the past (growled, spilled); milk has no plural.

options: A honest boy found a wallet and gave it to the teacher.
An honest boy found an wallet and gave it to the teacher.
An honest boy found a wallet and gave it to the teacher.
questions.rule: The h in honest is silent, so it starts with a vowel sound: an honest. But a wallet.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: seen
saw
sees

questions.rule: Last week and went show the past, so see becomes saw.

questions.prompt: One word is wrong. Find it and fix it.

options: are
am
was

questions.rule: Thousands of stars is plural, and it happens every night: there are.

questions.before: I wanted to see the Milky Way,
options: but
or
because of
questions.rule: The second idea goes against the first, so join them with but.

questions.after: a drink of milk, but he could not keep it.
options: wants
wanting
wanted
questions.rule: Could not is past, so the first verb is past too: wanted.
In a past question, did takes the past, so the main verb stays in base form: did ... spill.
Action first, then because + the reason.

chat: Did you finish the moon project?
options: Yes, I finish it, but I forgot the cover.
Yes, I finished it, but I forgetted the cover.
Yes, I finished it, but I forgot the cover.
questions.rule: Both parts are in the past: finished ... but ... forgot (not forgetted).

chat: Name one thing you saw at the science museum.
options: I saw an huge model of the Earth.
I saw a huge model of the Earth.
I saw a huge model of a Earth.
questions.rule: Huge begins with a consonant sound: a huge. There is only one Earth: the Earth.
